Coram: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Mohammad Nawaz
 Oral Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the appellant praying to enlarge him on bail in Crime No.47/2021 of Shahapur Police Station, wherein charge sheet is filed for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 302, 504 r/w 34 of IPC, Section 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) and 3(1)(s) of SC/ST (POA) Amendment Act, 2015.

2. Appellant is accused of committing the murder of his wife Jyothi by strangulating her with a rope,
in the rented house where they were residing, on 02.07.2021 between 9.30 a.m., and 8.40 p.m. NC:
2024:KHC-D:12870 3.
Challenging the rejection of the bail petition by the learned Sessions Judge, appellant had preferred Criminal Appeal No.100481/2021 before this Court.
The said appeal was dismissed on merits vide order dated 27.01.2022.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Appellant once again preferred a petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., to enlarge him on bail before the Sessions Court.
The learned Sessions Judge vide order dated 24.05.2022, in Criminal Misc No.576/2022 has dismissed the said petition.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the proceedings against accused Nos.2 to 4 have been quashed, by this Court in Crl.P No.102900/2022 on 19.04.2024, whereas the present appellant is languishing in judicial custody since 03.07.2021.
He submits that the charges are not yet framed, hence, there is delay in conducting the trial and therefore, sought to enlarge the appellant on bail.
The prayer of the appellant for bail has been opposed by the learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State.
7. While dismissing the earlier appeal, this Court has considered the entire facts and circumstances of the case.
The said appeal was dismissed on merits.

The learned Sessions Judge has also considered the nature and gravity of the offence and observing that the offence under Section 302 of IPC is punishable with death or imprisonment for life, declined to exercise the discretion in favour of the appellant.
8. Appellant is accused of committing a heinous offence.
Quashing of criminal proceedings against accused Nos.2 to 4 is not a ground to enlarge him on bail.
9. In so far as the delay in conducting trial is concerned, the appellant has not raised any such grounds before the trial Court.

Hence, appellant is at liberty to move the Sessions Court afresh under Section 439 of NC: 2024:KHC-D:12870 Cr.P.C., on any changed circumstances including the ground of delay if any in conducting the trial.
10. If any such application as mentioned above is filed, the learned Sessions Judge shall dispose of the same in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible.
With the above observation, the appeal is dismissed.

Sd/-
(MOHAMMAD NAWAZ) JUDGE HB/-
